summary: Sisir Roy works in philosophy and other fields, having studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He became a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute in 1993 and held a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies, attested in 2009.
Sita Krishna Nambiar worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Paul Hacker and held a position at Indraprastha College for Women.

Sita Ram Roy worked in Indology and history/archaeology, completing doctoral studies under Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma. He held posts at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Bihar, and Gaya Museum.
Siu-tong Kwan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and studied under teacher Zhihua Yao.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indologist. He held teaching posts at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, where he was attested as a Sanskrit teacher in 1892 and as an अध्यापक in 1929.

Sivan Goren Arzony is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She was attested as a PhD student at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2017 and as a Junior Fellow at Harvard University in 2020.
Siyong Liang (1904–1954) was an archaeologist and historian. He completed his education at Tsinghua University and Harvard University, where he studied around 1924 to 1930.

Smita Halder works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar and held an appointment as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

So Takahashi (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held posts at the University of Tokyo and Meijo University, serving as Associate Professor around 1977–1978 and professor in 1991.

Sodo Mori (born 1934) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Hajime Nakamura and others. He held professorships at Josai and Aichi Gakuin universities and posts at PTS and Kelaniya.
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Ekō Hashimoto and Kodo Sawaki, including training at Antai-ji between 1949 and 1957. He also taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and under Gempo Yamamoto. He taught Robert Baker Aitken, Maurine Stuart, Eido Shimano, Philip Kapleau, and John Daido Loori.

Sofija Aleksandrovna Černikova (1936–1995) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan and the University of Delhi, later teaching and serving as a Docent at the National University of Uzbekistan.

Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, and under Dokutan Sōsan and others. He served as a professor at Komazawa University and taught Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani and Philip Kapleau.
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Nihon University. He held a post at Kanagawa University and taught Koun Yamada and Kyozo Yamada.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Nihon University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot at Koho-in, was a professor and president at Hanazono University, and founded Chozen-ji.

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure who studied at Delhi and Cambridge, and under Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded Rigpa in 1975.
Sohini Sengupta works in Indology and other fields. She has been affiliated with the University of Chicago as a doctoral student, attested in 2024 and 2026.

Soiku Shigematsu (born 1943) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. In Buddhist studies and other fields, he held professorships at Shizuoka University and Kansai Medical University.

Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) worked in Buddhist studies. He was an assistant professor at Hanazono University, attested in 1974, served as 師家 at Zuigan-ji in the 1990s, and taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann.
